findings.claim: checkbox arms_running: 'Variant arms are live in the arena — 5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x' is green and marked critical.
findings.problem: The arena block lists seven arms in state running/confirm (sl-5pct, hold-12h, control, entry-8pct, placebo, tp-7pct, vol-4x), but this check counts only five, silently excluding control and placebo. The same check is the one asserting arms are live, so its own count disagrees with the registry it is reading — a metadata-over-evidence pattern (META) of exactly the firstred-1h kind. Whichever count is right, one of the two is wrong and no verdict should be issued until they agree.

findings.claim: placebo_inert: 'control n=1550 WR=49.9 · placebo n=1550 WR=49.9 · discordant pairs b=0 c=0 (must be 0/0 — placebo cannot change any decision)'.
findings.problem: This is established entirely on screen/backfill counts (n=1550 each) while the live tier holds only 50 events and both arms sit at live_n=13. Inertness proven on backfill does not establish inertness on the live tape, which is the only tier permitted to promote. The check is critical and green on evidence from a tier the project's own rule bars from deciding anything.

findings.claim: paired_population: 'Every arm scored on identical events — 4814 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them'.
findings.problem: The arena reports screen_n=496 for entry-8pct and screen_n=866 for vol-4x against screen_n=1550 for control, and declined=47 and 40 respectively versus 33. Seeing an event and scoring a trade on it are different things, but every arm-vs-arm statistic quoted here (screen_wr, screen_ev, screen_dWR) is computed on those unequal scored subsets, not on the 4814 shared events. The green check therefore does not establish that the reported comparisons are paired — the two filtered arms are being compared to control on populations that differ by construction.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is reported as running/confirm with screen_dWR=0.0pp, and vol-4x likewise with screen_dWR=0.0pp.
findings.problem: Both arms report a screen win rate different from control (51.613 and 51.27 vs control 49.935) yet a delta-WR of exactly 0.0pp, which cannot both be true if dWR is the arm-minus-control difference on the same window. Either the dWR field is not being computed for these arms or it is being computed against a different baseline; the project rule is to report delta vs the champion on the same window, and this field currently reports neither a valid delta nor an honest blank.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is a running confirm arm carrying live_n=3.
findings.problem: With measured ghost arrival at 25.2 control trades/day and a confirm target of n=600, an arm at live_n=3 while its same-cohort peers sit at live_n=13 is accumulating at a small fraction of the shared arrival rate. It is reported in the same running/confirm state as arms with four times its live sample, with no stated horizon; presenting it as an equal member of the arena overstates what it can decide, and its screen_ev=-0.055 is the only negative screen EV in the arena.

findings.claim: kernel_agreement is green at '195/200 live setups reproduced (97.5%)' and is marked critical.
findings.problem: Four of the five listed misses are the same coin (BOME, on four separate timestamps) and the fifth is BANANA — the failures are concentrated in specific names rather than randomly distributed, which is the signature of a systematic kernel gap on those coins, not of 2.5% random noise. A pass threshold of 90% on an aggregate rate cannot detect a per-coin systematic miss, so the green mark does not establish what the check is titled to establish.
